The only structure is a narrow brown cliff-edge strip on each side (rows 4-30, ending in a dark line at row 30) and green grass at the top corners. These strips are thin edge trims, not a front face under the ramp. The ramp itself is drawn as a flat top-down slope with no readable cut through a cliff face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown dirt ramp with wood-brown edge posts. It has about 3 main soil steps (light tan, mid brown, darker brown) plus a few speckles, against roughly 5-6 in the references. Its 7 visible tones per tile match the paving reference and beat the grass reference's 3, and its edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is dark brown beside the soil and wood, not sticker black. However, 13% near-flat coverage is the weak point: the reference grass and paving both measure 0%. By eye, the ramp body is broad, mostly flat tan with sparse grain, and it has few per-clump or per-stone highlights. It also lacks the cliff-face shading or ramp-slope gradient a careful artist would add. The result looks thinner and flatter than the references, so it reads as a simple fill with a few dots.
